subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Steam Locomotive: Rails Change Everything
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Steam Locomotive: Rails Change Everything.

hook.text: In 1804 a steam engine rolled on iron rails for the first time.

buildup.text: A boiler made steam. Pistons turned wheels. The locomotive pulled wagons.

discovery.text: Steel wheels on steel rails have ultra-low friction — one engine pulls tons.

twist.text: Stephenson's Rocket won the Rainhill Trials and proved trains were practical.

climax.text: Within 50 years, railroads connected entire continents and reshaped nations.

punchline.text: Put an engine on rails and distance shrinks forever.

quiz.question: Why can one locomotive pull so much weight?
options: Steam engines produce unlimited torque at low speed
Steel wheels on steel rails create very low rolling friction
The weight of the locomotive pushes the rails down to reduce friction
